Gene Description

CASP8 is a tandem-death-effector-domain initiator caspase that couples receptor and cytosolic signaling complexes to cell-death outcomes. Procaspase-8 is recruited to FADD-containing death-inducing signaling complexes and ripoptosomes, where proximity-induced dimerization and autoproteolysis generate an Asp-directed cysteine endopeptidase. Active CASP8 initiates extrinsic apoptosis by maturing effector caspases, cleaves RIPK1 and RIPK3 to restrain necroptosis and inflammatory TNF signaling, and can route inflammasome or death-receptor inputs into gasdermin-mediated pyroptosis by maturing gasdermin-family substrates directly or through CASP3. CASP8 also has catalysis-independent DED-scaffold and phosphorylation-dependent migration roles, and several short isoforms lacking the catalytic domain antagonize death-receptor apoptosis.

Core Functions

CASP8 is recruited to FADD-containing death-inducing signaling complexes and matures downstream effector caspases to initiate extrinsic apoptotic signaling.

Molecular Function:
cysteine-type endopeptidase activity
Directly Involved In:
extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway via death domain receptors
Cellular Locations:
cytosol
In Complex:
death-inducing signaling complex

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: Should CASP8 gasdermin cleavage be represented as direct gasdermin protein maturation, as regulation of pyroptotic inflammatory response, or only in GO-CAMs where the input gasdermin is explicit?

Q: Which CASP8 immune-differentiation and developmental phenotypes should remain as flat GO biological-process annotations rather than being modeled through the more direct RIPK1/necroptosis checkpoint?

Q: Should catalysis-independent CASP8 migration signaling at lamellipodia receive a specific molecular-function term distinct from cysteine endopeptidase activity and death-effector-domain binding?

Suggested Experiments

Experiment: Introduce separation-of-function mutations into the CASP8 tandem DEDs in a CASP8-null human epithelial or lymphoid line, then quantify DISC recruitment, effector-caspase maturation, RIPK1 cleavage, and necroptosis after FASL, TRAIL, and TNF stimulation.

Hypothesis: CASP8 DED interfaces that recruit FADD and cFLIP differentially control extrinsic apoptosis versus RIPK1 cleavage.

Type: structure-function pathway assay

Experiment: Use cells expressing noncleavable endogenous GSDMC, GSDMD, or GSDME variants together with acute CASP8 rescue or inhibition to measure direct cleavage, pore formation, and cytokine release after DR6, TAK1/NLRP1, and TNF inputs.

Hypothesis: CASP8 directly determines which gasdermin substrate is matured in epithelial pyroptotic responses.

Type: gasdermin cleavage rescue assay

📚 Additional Documentation

Notes

(CASP8-notes.md)

CASP8 notes

2026-09-30

  • Seeded and completed the human CASP8 review from GOA, UniProt, cached PubMed
    records, Reactome, GO-CAM models, and PAINT transfer context.
  • Kept the CASP8 core centered on three direct mechanisms: FADD/death-effector
    domain recruitment to death-inducing signaling complexes, Asp-directed
    cysteine endopeptidase activity that matures downstream procaspases and
    gasdermin substrates, and RIPK1 cleavage that restrains RIPK1/RIPK3-dependent
    necroptosis.
  • Tightened top-level GO:0006915 apoptotic process assertions toward
    death-domain receptor extrinsic apoptotic signaling, while leaving the
    abstract-only PMID:22891283 Fas vesicle row UNDECIDED.
  • Moved CASP8 away from effector-only GO:0097194 execution phase of apoptosis
    wording. CASP8 is an initiator that activates CASP3/CASP7 and other
    substrates by proteolytic maturation; CASP3 and CASP7 carry the direct
    executioner role.
  • Removed all 94 generic GO:0005515 protein binding rows. The FADD/CFLAR/FAS
    edges were either already represented by specific death-effector-domain or
    DISC annotations, and the BioPlex, binary-interactome, viral-inhibitor, and
    other screen edges did not identify a CASP8-specific molecular activity.
  • Removed the impossible Ensembl electronic GO:0030690 Noc1p-Noc2p complex
    mapping to human CASP8, together with stimulus-response and assay-readout rows
    that did not establish direct CASP8 work.
  • Kept pyroptosis, dectin-1 inflammasome, TLR3/TLR4 ripoptosome, N4BP1 innate
    immune, and host-pathogen perturbation rows as non-core where they captured
    real CASP8-containing complexes or substrate-cleavage branches.
  • Deferred rows whose visible cached evidence was abstract-only, review-derived,
    or centered on a different caspase or readout, including the
    HSP70/GATA1 localization rows, the COP/CARD-only protein paper, the
    CAAP/C9orf82 paper, the p23 paper, and specific immune differentiation terms
    sourced only to PMID:18309324.

id: Q14790
gene_symbol: CASP8
product_type: PROTEIN
status: COMPLETE
taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:9606
  label: Homo sapiens
description: 'CASP8 is a tandem-death-effector-domain initiator caspase that couples receptor and cytosolic signaling complexes
  to cell-death outcomes. Procaspase-8 is recruited to FADD-containing death-inducing signaling complexes and ripoptosomes,
  where proximity-induced dimerization and autoproteolysis generate an Asp-directed cysteine endopeptidase. Active CASP8 initiates
  extrinsic apoptosis by maturing effector caspases, cleaves RIPK1 and RIPK3 to restrain necroptosis and inflammatory TNF
  signaling, and can route inflammasome or death-receptor inputs into gasdermin-mediated pyroptosis by maturing gasdermin-family
  substrates directly or through CASP3. CASP8 also has catalysis-independent DED-scaffold and phosphorylation-dependent migration
  roles, and several short isoforms lacking the catalytic domain antagonize death-receptor apoptosis.'

    caspases to initiate extrinsic apoptotic signaling.

proposed_new_terms: []
suggested_questions:
- question: Should CASP8 gasdermin cleavage be represented as direct gasdermin protein maturation, as regulation of
    pyroptotic inflammatory response, or only in GO-CAMs where the input gasdermin is explicit?
  experts: []
- question: Which CASP8 immune-differentiation and developmental phenotypes should remain as flat GO biological-process
    annotations rather than being modeled through the more direct RIPK1/necroptosis checkpoint?
  experts: []
- question: Should catalysis-independent CASP8 migration signaling at lamellipodia receive a specific molecular-function
    term distinct from cysteine endopeptidase activity and death-effector-domain binding?
  experts: []
suggested_experiments:
- hypothesis: CASP8 DED interfaces that recruit FADD and cFLIP differentially control extrinsic apoptosis versus RIPK1
    cleavage.
  description: Introduce separation-of-function mutations into the CASP8 tandem DEDs in a CASP8-null human epithelial or
    lymphoid line, then quantify DISC recruitment, effector-caspase maturation, RIPK1 cleavage, and necroptosis after
    FASL, TRAIL, and TNF stimulation.
  experiment_type: structure-function pathway assay
- hypothesis: CASP8 directly determines which gasdermin substrate is matured in epithelial pyroptotic responses.
  description: Use cells expressing noncleavable endogenous GSDMC, GSDMD, or GSDME variants together with acute CASP8
    rescue or inhibition to measure direct cleavage, pore formation, and cytokine release after DR6, TAK1/NLRP1, and TNF
    inputs.
  experiment_type: gasdermin cleavage rescue assay
